info.name: Internal Wallet Transactional System API
info.description:
# Internal Wallet API

Postman requests for the Rails JSON API. Start the Rails server, create a provisioned user and wallets, import the Local environment, select it, then use the Auth, Wallets, and Transactions folders in order.

## Important behavior
- This is an API-only app; there is no signup endpoint.
- Only IDR wallets are supported. Amounts are decimal strings with at most two fractional digits.
- Deposit directly credits the user's own internal wallet. It is not connected to a bank, card, or payment provider.
- Withdrawal debits the user's own wallet; it does not send money to an external account.
- Transfers debit only the signed-in user's wallet and may credit any existing wallet. Team and Stock wallets may receive transfers but cannot be debited through this API.
- Every transaction request needs a unique `Idempotency-Key`. Reusing a key with the same actor and same request returns the original transaction; changing the payload with the same key returns `409 idempotency_conflict`. Change the key when changing the amount or wallet IDs.
- After sign-in, Postman stores the `wallet_session` cookie automatically. The sign-in test script saves `data.csrf_token` into the selected environment as `csrfToken`; authenticated POST/DELETE requests send it as `X-CSRF-Token`. Keep using the same hostname (`localhost` vs `127.0.0.1`) so Postman sends the cookie.
- A transfer response returns `source_balance` only. It deliberately does not reveal the target wallet balance.

## Common error format
`{ "error": { "code": "...", "message": "..." } }`

Common codes: `unauthorized` (401), `forbidden` / `csrf_invalid` (403), `not_found` (404), `validation_error` / `insufficient_funds` (422), and `idempotency_conflict` (409).

item.name: Health
item.description: Check that Rails is running. This endpoint does not require authentication.

request.description: Expected: HTTP 200 when the app is healthy.

item.name: Authentication
item.description: Sign in with a user created by an administrator. No signup route is available.

exec: pm.test('CSRF token was saved to the selected environment', function () { pm.expect(body.data.csrf_token).to.be.a('string').and.not.empty; });

request.description:
Creates a session for an existing user. On success, the server sets `wallet_session` (HTTP-only) and `wallet_csrf` cookies and returns a CSRF token. Postman keeps the cookies in its cookie jar; the test script saves the CSRF token into the selected environment.

Success: `201 Created`. Invalid credentials: `401` with error code `unauthorized`.
Returns the signed-in user's ID and email. Requires the session cookie. Success: `200 OK`; missing, expired, or revoked session: `401 unauthorized`.
Revokes the current database session and clears both auth cookies. Requires the session cookie and CSRF header. Success: `204 No Content`. Sign in again before making more authenticated requests.

item.name: Wallets
item.description: Wallet reads are limited to wallets owned by the signed-in user. Wallet creation is not exposed over this API.

request.description: Returns wallet ID, currency, and ledger-derived balance. Set `sourceWalletId` to a wallet owned by the signed-in user. Success: `200`; another user's wallet: `403`; unknown ID: `404`.

Returns up to 100 newest ledger entries for a wallet owned by the signed-in user. Each item includes the signed amount, transaction ID/type, and creation time. Positive amounts credit the wallet; negative amounts debit it.

item.name: Transactions
item.description: All transaction writes require a valid session cookie, `X-CSRF-Token`, and a unique `Idempotency-Key`. Use decimal amounts such as `"25.00"`; values with more than two decimal places are rejected. Wallet balance is derived from ledger entries.

exec: if (pm.response.code === 201) { pm.test('Response contains a transaction ID', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().data.id).to.be.a('number'); }); }

request.description: Credits the signed-in user's own wallet and creates a positive ledger entry. This endpoint represents an internal credit only; it is not connected to a payment gateway. Success: `201 Created` with transaction data and the wallet's new balance.

Debits the signed-in user's own wallet by creating a negative ledger entry. There is no external payout. The amount cannot exceed the ledger-derived balance. Insufficient balance returns `422 insufficient_funds`. Success: `201 Created` with the new balance.

exec: pm.test('Response does not disclose target balance', function () { pm.expect(data).not.to.have.property('target_balance'); });

request.description: Debits the signed-in user's wallet and credits any existing target wallet, including a User, Team, or Stock wallet. The source must belong to the signed-in user; the target ID must exist. Success: `201 Created`, with balanced signed ledger entries and the source balance. The target balance is intentionally omitted.

item.name: Error and idempotency examples
item.description: Optional requests for trying common errors. Restore the amount/key after experiments before running the normal flow again.

request.description: Intentionally omits `X-CSRF-Token`. With an active session, expected response is `403` and code `csrf_invalid`. No ledger entry is written.
Intentionally uses three decimal places. Expected response is `422 validation_error`; no transaction is committed.
